newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Wesfarmers to build A$150 mln ammonia plant.
newsitem.headline: Wesfarmers to build A$150 mln ammonia plant.

text.p: Diversified Australian rural, chemicals and energy group Wesfarmers Ltd said on Tuesday that it would build an ammonia plant at Kwinana in Western Australia at a cost of A$150 million (US$114 million).
The plant would produce 650 tonnes a day of the key industrial chemical, more than double Wesfarmers' current capacity, and replace 100,000 tonnes of imported product a year, the company said.
It said construction of the plant would begin in the second quarter of 1998 and it would be commissioned in the third quarter of 1999.

Wesfarmers said the project was expected to make a significant contribution to the group's results from 1999 onwards, and would be financed from the group's internal cash flow and existing loan facilities.

Ammonia is a key raw material in the manufacture of ammonium nitrate, used to make explosives for the mining industry, and nitrogenous fertilisers for agriculture. It is also used in the production of sodium cyanide, an essential reagent used in the gold extraction process, and in nickel refining.

Peter Knowles, managing director of the group's fertiliser and chemical subsidiary Wesfarmers CSBP Ltd, said the company had experienced strong growth in demand for these three major downstream products and that demand for use in nickel refining was expected to grow.
"The new plant will provide competitively priced and secure supplies of ammonia and other downstream products to Western Australia's mining and agricultural sectors," he said in a statement.
The plant will be designed and built on a turnkey basis by the Italian engineering company Technipetrol SpA using technology licensed from Haldor Topsoe of Denmark.
